title: The Teacher as Food and the Transformation of the Soul
english: They say: 'You turned us backward among our enemies' (Ps 44:23). And those hating us seized us for themselves (Ps 44:24). They would not have been able to take us by hand, if you had not turned us back among them for the sake of usefulness. They are enemies and haters; for to hate is to be an enemy. But we are neither enemies nor haters. And because of this we were far off; for what judgment... Lord, you turned us back among them, you have made us to be with those who are condemned. Therefore, those who were formerly in the form of God, having taken the form of a slave through compassion, say such a thing: that we have come to an earthly place not for ourselves, but for the sake of others, because you did not go out in our powers; for formerly you used to go out in our powers to bring us the victory against our enemies, and guarding us in the land of our fathers where we descended. Since therefore you did not go out in our powers, we were turned backward among those hating us. Those having seized us, to whom you gave—but with a bad intention... And you find many such things in the Scripture; from envy... him in action. But they did not crucify him with this intention. Again Judas betrayed the Savior, and the betrayal became useful for the removal of 'the sin of the world' (John 1:29). Again, those crucifying did not crucify him with this intention. 'Those hating us seized us for themselves' (Ps 44:24), they did not kill us. But if you say this, that they took our things for their own profit, and that the betrayal and the turning backward occurred timely. Therefore they bring forward: 'All these things came upon us, and we did not remember you' (Ps 44:26). You gave us as sheep for feeding (Ps 44:25). Formerly you helped openly so that our praise would be to you all day long and to confess in your name forever. But why now have we been delivered into captivity, suffering this not because of our wickedness or impiety? Those saying the psalm were such as Daniel... the one of Joshua and Ezekiel and Haggai and Zechariah and the three and others more. These are...

Not because of personal malice has one become in Babylon. But concerning those handed over to afflictions, and especially those in whom the choice is precarious because they rejoice over those handed over through malice, they were sent like physicians after wars, so that they might care for them, bringing aids that either preserve their existing health or dissolve disease and bring health.

For it is not, as some suppose, that they blame that day. Instead, they move toward other sayings: 'You have given us as sheep for food' (Ps 54:2). We were handed over for our own eating; lions and wolves are devouring us. However, even if we are being devoured, we do not cease to be sheep: 'Israel was a wandering sheep; lions drove him out; the first devoured him, the King of Assyria' (Hos 11:7, 10:6). It is a bad thing for what has happened to be praised, not to remain as it is, but to be resolved into another quality. The one eating bread, if he sends it down into the stomach, the bread does not remain. And those who have been cast down and have become the food of enemies have not ceased to be sheep.

It is often said that food becomes the disciple of the teacher, concerning whom he also says: 'My food is to do the will of Him who sent me' (John 4:34). The Samaritan woman was indeed a disciple, concerning whom he also said: 'I have food to eat which you do not know' (John 4:32). [Gaps in text] ... and again [Gaps] ... to be bread. And bread becomes nourishment. In a certain way [Gaps] ...

If, therefore, the man who preserves the image and the likeness, having become a teacher of God according to Jesus, eats a wild man through the process of training [Gaps] ... and having become food for the teacher, he shall not be a lion. For this reason, he is blessed and is called blessed, not because he is a lion, but because he has become a man. But if ever a rational man, moving rationally, were to be eaten by a violent wild man or an evil power, he becomes a lion and such a one is a terror; for 'woe to the man whom the lion eats' (Job 15:26). These therefore say: 'You gave us as sheep for food.' Having been eaten as sheep, they remained [sheep]. And among the nations you scattered us. According to the immediate sense of the word...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Bondage of Sin and the Substitutions of Sacrifice
english: They seem to say this: 'We have been sown among the nations, we have been dispersed in many places.' But they seem to have suffered this in Babylon and Assyria alone. Therefore, what he says is this: the sowing of these seeds, such as wheat or barley, is first useful in a Gospel-like way if they are sown in the earth; for this earth receives them into its own substance through a change and transformation. For from the earth, having changed, many came from one grain; they changed from the earth into harvests. It is animated... [gap]... into the adjacent earth, and it notifies it and transforms it into its own nature.

And he says 'seeds' regarding those saying these things, the saints, saying: 'In you we shall be praised and in your name we shall confess for ever' (Ps 111:3, 9). Behold, those saying: 'With you we horn our enemies' and the others, let them say: 'You have sown us among the nations' by way of seeds, so that the nations, in a certain way, if we are sown among them in a foreign land, we might change into ourselves, and one of us might become an ear of corn bearing many grains, benefiting many souls. And those being benefited are said to be different: sometimes children of those benefiting, when those are named fathers, sometimes sheep, when those have the state and conduct of a shepherd. These therefore, as seeds having been cast down, took into themselves those being benefited from being placed before them. Having been placed, the seeds changed the earth. The nations therefore are the earth, but the seeds are those cast down for the benefit of others. Let this also be simpler: that the Assyrians have become in Babylon, though they are not many nations and all the nations are. And let this also be toward my history.

13 You sent away your people without honor (Ps 79:2). Without honor... [gap]... sent away; for having been led into captivity, we were not led there with honor, but having been led by the law of captivity; for nothing is more dishonorable than this. 'Without honor' therefore [is] 'you sent away your people'. [gap]... the people whom they wished to hold. And it is possible also to call that people, for whom... [gap]... among the others. And since 'you sent away your people without honor', that is, not having received honor, 'you sent away', [gap]... them; for they were given over to their own sins. And it is possible also that 'without honor'...

And for this reason we have endured these things, to come into captivity and to be scattered among the nations, so that you might gather to yourself. He has done to himself through sin and has made himself a debtor.

Furthermore, the thing by which the enemy, the king of souls, holds [us], is called a handwriting. And a handwriting is something which someone has fastened with his own hands. Therefore 'he took it out from the middle,' so that it might no longer hold us by the handwriting with which we had fastened ourselves, having written ourselves down in it. And are they also being written down together with themselves? —that is, us being your people, you sent away without honor (Ps 79:9)—then we were honored—by the manner of the captivity; or they speak concerning the people, for whom they themselves went into captivity: 'You sent away your people without honor' (Ps 79:9). And for this reason we endure these things, because for the sake of their help you made the same things for them to draw from again, unpleasantly.

And there was not a multitude in our substitutions. Often, for the sake of certain things, safe and redeeming substitutions are given. For instance, it says: 'It is holy everything that opens a male womb.' And it says that, if it is a firstborn sheep or an ox or a goat, among those brought to the altar, it is necessary to perform the sacrifice itself. But if it is a firstborn donkey or something else [of the priests], it is not even brought to the altar; 'you shall change a sheep in its place.' Through a sheep its value is changed and it enters into the temple. He says therefore that, since there were many, 'there was not a multitude in their substitutions.' There were not so many substitutions so that... in this way that, since God is the one giving the substitutions in their place, the substitutions are given being changed. And through a few, he is able to nourish many-peopled multitudes. And so that I may speak from history, there were many people, and if ten righteous men were found there (Ezek 14:14)—for until they... there being no multitude of substitutions, they were being changed. No one will say, therefore, to Babylon, [but] few in number as the...

title: The Nature of Reproach and the Mustard Seed
english: Having been taken captive together... themselves and the people, and those others through sin, but the people through their own [sins] and the others through the [sins] of others. 'And there was not a multitude in their leaps' (Jonah 3:4). But few had become sufficient for... it would have happened, if they had turned back and known what evils they are in. 'Their sins are very great; I will go down and see if they have worked according to their cry coming toward me, but if not, so that I may know' (Jonah 4:2). How much [it reached] upon the cry of their wickedness and the... but if I do not find them such, but having repented like the Ninevites, I will know them. For those known by God are not trivial; 'the Lord knew those who were His' (1 Sam 2:30). 'But then, not knowing God, you served gods which are not gods by nature; but now, having known God, rather having been known by God' (Acts 17:29). When they were knowing, they were rather being known by the Benefactor.

14 A reproach has become to us from our neighbors. Regarding the history, the neighbors are the nearby ones... since therefore we were carried off into captivity, 'a reproach we have become to our neighbors' (Ps 147:2). They themselves have not suffered nor have they prevailed with the rising of wars, but we. And as for the thought of this: just as the cross of the Savior has become a reproach for the sake of salvation—for it has been said: 'counting the reproach of Christ a greater wealth than the treasures of Egypt' (Ex 12:33)—so also these have in a way fallen into reproaches, having been seized and having been led into captivity. 'Angels,' he says, 'who did not keep their own beginning, but having left their own habitation, fell into everlasting chains' (Heb 2:16). This reproach of the angels is not praiseworthy, because having been granted to dwell in heaven and being able to stand and remain beside God always praising, they became in wickedness so as to fall from heaven. This reproach is trivial. Behold, indeed, the [reproach] of Christ is not only praiseworthy, but is greater than treasures. And if there were no difference between these, the proverbist would not have said: 'Do not acquire the reproach of evil men' (Prov 22:1). When therefore the apostles [were] rejoicing...

They rejoice even while being reproached for Christ. Having done nothing [wrong], these reproaches of such people are not good. By becoming reproach itself, someone has established the practice of reproaching based on false accusations, not on truths. Thus also is the saying, 'We are without honor; for I think God has shown us the apostles to be the very last, as if marked for death' (1 Cor 4:9). This is the reproach in which they are placed. It is not a true reproach, nor is it from evil men, but from good men. Regarding the spoken word: that it is not earnest, nor God-fearing, and that those coming are our enemies, yet they did not drive us from their land.

14 They mock and deride us in our circle. The ones saying they have come not for their own sake, but for the sake of others, are holy. And they say: having been born, having held us and having drawn us into their land, being in our circle, they reproach us, mock us, and sneer at us; but the reproach, the mockery, and the derision do not touch us, but them. Just as if someone derides [another], so that they may have children by weaving themselves together, and enjoy [themselves]. Therefore, those who are being mocked by these are thought to be [such].

15 He made us a parable among the nations. Something hidden by a word is compared to something similar. That it may become clear, let us see from the Gospel (Matt 13:31): he compares the kingdom of heaven to a mustard seed, not saying 'it is like a mustard seed' while being a seed itself; for it was no longer a similarity, but an identity. He says 'hyper' [beyond/exceeding]. Therefore, the mustard seed has a power smaller in size than the seeds, capable of transforming and becoming such a plant. And the kingdom of heaven, thus revealing the teaching of the Scriptures, is something humble and small in its wording.
